newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO says meeting with Israel possible in Malta.
newsitem.headline: PLO says meeting with Israel possible in Malta.

text.p: The PLO on Monday dampened Israeli expectations of a meeting between Foreign Minister David Levy and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat at European-Mediterranean talks in Malta.
But a senior PLO official said Levy might meet Palestinian Planning and International Cooperation Minister Nabil Shaath at the two-day conference starting on Tuesday.

"There are efforts under way to convene a Palestinian-Israeli meeting and the meeting may take place between Shaath and Levy," Ahmed Abdel-Rahman, director-general of the Palestinian Authority, told Voice of Palestine radio.

Palestinian and Israeli officials said the European Union's Middle East envoy, Miguel Angel Moratinos, was at the centre of efforts to arrange an Israeli-PLO meeting in Malta to defuse the current crisis in peace efforts.

"We received a message from Mr Moratinos, the European envoy, about an interest by ... Mr Arafat and Mr Abu Mazen to meet with the foreign minister," Israeli Foreign Ministry director-general Eytan Bentsur said.
"When the foreign minister arrives in Malta and if the approach is made, I estimate he will take a positive view (of such a meeting)," he told Israel Radio.
But PLO officials said Arafat, who was consulting with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Cairo on Monday before going to Malta, has ruled out a meeting with Levy at this stage.
Arafat aide Nabil Abu Rdainah told Reuters: "There won't be any meeting with Levy during the Malta conference."

The Middle East peace process ground to a halt after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gave the green light for the start of the construction of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18.

Three days later, a Moslem bomber blew up a Tel Aviv cafe, killing himself and three Israeli women. Netanyahu said peace talks would not resume until Arafat cracked down on "terrorism". Arafat said Israel must stop the East Jerusalem project.
Countries attending the two-day conference are to discuss advancing the 27-member EU-Mediterranean Partnership created in Barcelona in 1995.

Israeli commentators said Levy was concerned Arab states would use the forum to criticise Israel for its settlement of occupied land but EU council president Hans van Mierlo said the Arabs have agreed not to raise the issue.
Palestinians view East Jerusalem as the capital of their future state and say the settlement violates international law. Israel claims all of Jerusalem as its capital.

Arafat told reporters at Cairo airport before heading to talks with Mubarak that they would discuss how to protect peace "particularly in light of continued Israeli efforts to break the agreements signed in Washington and Cairo."
